assessments.critic_note: Novelty verified (2 independent search passes): no version-matched comparison of the population of reported statistics exists. But lit_against is presented as complete and is not: it omits Nuijten & Wicherts, AMPPS 2024 (preregistered quasi-experiment, >7,000 articles / >147,000 statistics, statcheck-adopting vs matched control journals, steeper decline in decision inconsistencies near p=.05), which partly pre-answers the 'does review repair inconsistencies' sub-question at journal level, and Sci Rep 2023 (10.1038/s41598-023-44291-4; 329 medRxiv prevention preprints, 16.8% changed primary-outcome effect magnitude) which is a closer pair study than the 547-pair Bero study it leans on. I verified the load-bearing access claim myself: ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/pmc/preprints/ serves exactly the 8 shards + pprid.txt.gz the scout lists, byte-range fetch 206 OK. Two calibration problems: (1) PreprintToPaper (now in Scientific Data) is bioRxiv-centred, while the hypothesis names bioRxiv AND medRxiv - medRxiv coverage must be verified before plan.md is committed or the >=10,000-pair denominator may not exist; (2) biomedical papers yield far fewer statcheck-parseable triples than psychology, and the scout's own risks concede the sample may fall below 10,000. 7 -> 6: the question is actively contested but the design is power-limited and the 67% threshold is asserted, not derived. Cost 4 stands (25 GB, CPU-only, verified sizes).

Not answered, but much closer prior art than the scout found: 'Born Flawed? Publication-Time Citation Topology Improves Retraction Early-Warning' (Research Square rs-10177352, doi 10.21203/rs.3.rs-10177352/v1) reports publication-time features, explicit leakage control and an OUT-OF-TIME protocol with a +0.176 [0.099,0.252] gain and a triage framing - i.e. the hindcast limb (H1) may already be done. I could not read the full text (Research Square is JS-gated; WebFetch returned title only), so this is a hard precondition rather than a cut: the lead must not be preregistered until that preprint is obtained and lit_against rewritten around it. Also omitted: Venturini et al., arXiv:2604.02302 (2026), which supplies the 0.12% cohort base rate the design needs. Value 7 -> 5: with Born Flawed in view, only the base-rate-honest true-cohort framing and the sealed 2028 forward forecast are clearly new. Cost 6 -> 7 and feasibility local -> stretch: 120 GB claimed is optimistic for an OpenAlex works-parquet pass plus PubMed baseline plus a PMC content block on ~200 GB free NVMe (column-selective fetching is mandatory, not optional); Retraction Watch via Crossref Labs is confirmed slow but usable (I measured 8.1 MB streamed in 120 s, no 502); and the scoring step sits in Dec 2028, two years past every other pending obligation this lab holds. Power is marginal by the scout's own arithmetic (0.1% base rate, top-1% stratum of a 1M cohort = a few hundred expected events), so a power calculation must precede commitment.

Census limb is open - no one has measured retraction markers inside the distributed artefacts (PMC OA bulk XML, Europe PMC preprint bulk, peS2o). Two omissions matter: the CRAN package 'retraction' v0.1.0 (Jul 2026) already checks JATS XML and reference lists against Retraction Watch/Crossref/OpenAlex, which substantially undercuts the constructive 'drop-in overlay' selling point, and Illinois Data Bank IDB-5333456 (208 DOIs that lost their Crossref retracted flag between Apr 2023 and Jul 2024) already measures flag instability, overlapping the latency arm. Access verified: Retraction Watch via Crossref Labs streams (slow, no error), PMC OA S3 anonymous, peS2o ungated. Value 6 -> 5: the scout's own risks concede the pilot suggests live Europe PMC records ARE well marked, so the >50%-unmarked primary is likely refuted; that is still worth running, but as a measurement with the latency and derived-corpus numbers carrying it, not as a headline. Cost 5 stands. Before start: check what the 'retraction' package already does and reposition the overlay as an evaluation of it rather than a new artefact.

CUT - answered, and the scout's novelty claim is not honest. Nguyen, McKenzie, Alqaidoom, Hamilton, Moher & Page, 'Reproducibility of meta-analytic results in systematic reviews of interventions', BMJ Medicine 2025;4:e002024 (PMC12684188) uses this lead's exact design and exact criterion. I verified the abstract directly: 121 index meta-analyses, recomputed predominantly from the study-level numbers printed in the article (only 19% of authors supplied data), 'fully reproducible' defined as <10% difference in summary estimate and CI width - 104/121 (86%) fully reproducible, 7 (6%) not, 10 (8%) insufficient information, zero meaningful differences, 1/65 significance-category shifts and that one did not cross 0.05; 23% at a 5% tolerance. The lead's primary (>=15% irreproducible to within 10%, excluding inconclusive) is therefore pre-refuted at ~6-14%. The lit_against asserts nobody has 'recomputed pooled estimates from the forest-plot tables that open-access meta-analyses already print' and cites only Maassen 2020; it also omits Gotzsche et al. (37% non-replicable, the original of the design), the 2025 ecology/evolution reliability study (PMC12092126, 41 MAs / 5,703 effect sizes) and Hamilton et al., Research Synthesis Methods 2026. The only residue is scale (population vs 121; all pooled estimates vs the index one) with a prior that predicts a null - not worth three weeks. Scores recorded for the record only.

Novelty holds - no published count of TK/BC Label or Notice uptake, and no crosswalk-fidelity measurement, anywhere. I independently reproduced the scout's enabling census myself: api.datacite.org query rightsList.rightsUri:*localcontexts* returns total=48,351 today, and localcontextshub.org/projects/ serves 200 as public HTML (the 403 Hub API is genuinely routed around). That reproducibility is exactly the problem: see ruling_prereg_integrity. Value 6 -> 4: once the DataCite census is correctly treated as a scouting result, the preregistered residue is a descriptive count across named non-DataCite platforms plus a crosswalk matrix - useful, cheap, but not a 6, and the 99.96%-single-prefix concentration means all population statistics describe one publisher's bulk mint (Neotoma). Cost 2 stands (3 GB, 3-4 days). Before start: check Creative Commons + Local Contexts, 'Guidance for Indigenous Collections and Data' (English final, Sep 2026) for any published counts, and note the Dataverse dc:rights/oai_dc crosswalk-loss issues (#8129, #5920/#4176) as prior art for the H2 mechanism. needs_engagement correctly present.

Strongest novelty in the batch: three independent searches found nothing that tests whether a model surfaces a rights element it was given, and nothing with an Indigenous-governance arm; the closest adjacent work (LLM licence EXTRACTION into rights vocabularies; LLM4RE, arXiv 2510.18787) is weaker than the scout's own lit_against. Model access verified ungated. Value 7 -> 6, not lower: it is a real, actively relevant gap, but the treatment arm is dominated by one publisher and one Notice type ('Open to Collaborate'), so the result may be about one phrase, and three open-weight models do not represent the hosted assistants researchers actually use. Cost 3 -> 4: Qwen3-32B at bf16 is ~64 GB on an 80 GB A100 that is shared with the owner's vLLM container - the plan must commit to FP8/AWQ or to freeing the GPU for the stage, not assume headroom. Two conditions: (a) the engagement dependency is a genuine start gate, not a publication gate - the rubric is the study and the lab cannot author it alone, so this lead's schedule is bounded by a human process it does not control; (b) all inference must stay on local open-weight models so TK/BC-labelled metadata is never transmitted to a third-party API - currently implied, must be explicit in plan.md.

Novelty holds on independent search: nothing stratifies gridded-rainfall skill by per-cell gauge support, uses gauge-blended/satellite-only twins as a design, or covers PICTs beyond Fiji. One correction the gap must absorb: the Fiji 2026 paper the scout already cites in lit_for (10.1007/s00704-026-06197-9) evaluates both CHIRP_V1 and CHIRPS_v2.0 and reports satellite-only products agreeing BETTER on small isolated islands - i.e. the twin comparison exists at one site and already points the lead's way, so the twin design cannot be sold as untouched. CHIRPS3/CHIRP3 (Sci Data 2026) is a new enabler worth adding. Value 7 -> 6: a genuine methodological blind spot in products used for PICT climate services, with a clean falsifiable null, but several PICTs have one or two stations and short records, and 'independent' is only a proxy (national services may have supplied data through channels GPCC counts miss) - the scout is honest about both, which caps the achievable claim. Cost 5 stands; 90 GB is plausible but at the optimistic end for CHIRP daily global GeoTIFFs plus CMORPH plus PERSIANN plus ERA5. All eight endpoints are open HTTP; the ERA5 route via the NSF-NCAR S3 mirror correctly avoids the CDS account. needs_engagement (SPREP/SPC) correctly present and genuinely load-bearing, since country-level skill statements are the output.

The recovery limb (H3) is substantially narrowed by prior art the scout missed: GeoBoost2 (Bioinformatics 36(20):5120, 2020) is precisely 'recover geographic origin for GenBank records from the linked publication', with a deployed service, and it now has an independent 2026 benchmark (Bioinformatics Advances 6(1):vbag225) reporting 79% sensitivity with an 89% false-positive rate and 55% macro-F1 over 129 articles - which makes the lead's '>=40% recall at >=90% precision' target look optimistic and makes EnvMine (2010) a stale precision benchmark to cite. H1 (the May-2023 INSDC mandate as a record-level discontinuity) and H2 (placeholder decomposition at archive scale) are genuinely open; CBD SBI-07 materials confirm no baseline exists. Value 7 -> 5: the contribution reduces to the discontinuity measurement plus an honest placeholder taxonomy, with the recovery limb reframed as a reproduction of GeoBoost2-class performance. Cost 4 -> 5 (BioSample XML alone is 4.95 GB gzipped, verified by the scout; with ENA and the PubMed baseline the 60 GB estimate is right at the band boundary). Governance: the human-sample exclusion at the first filter is the correct design; needs_engagement correctly present, and plan.md must additionally commit to publishing no taxon- or collection-level result for taonga species and no country-level compliance finding.

Novelty holds: no detection-or-power test of the SEAPODYM redistribution trend exists; searches return projections (Bell 2021, FAO/Common Oceans) and short-record ENSO/CPUE work only. The access trap is genuinely routed around and I verified it myself rather than taking the scout's word: the WCPFC public-domain 1x1-degree monthly file downloads anonymously from SPC's THREDDS fileServer at 1,619,785,634 bytes, and the SEAPODYM 2DEG catalogue XML serves 200 - no registration anywhere in the path. Worth adding: Dutta (2025), 'Vessel Day Scheme and Tuna Catch in the Pacific Island Region' (10.1002/app5.70042) and WCPFC's own 2025 Commission descriptive EEZ shares (~88% of 2024 catch inside coastal EEZs) as the baseline series. Value 7 -> 6: the 13%-loss figure genuinely drives Pacific fisheries policy and a power result would be used, but the scout's own risks concede that public-domain cells with low vessel counts are zeroed out in exactly the sparse small EEZs the hypothesis is about, and that purse-seine CPUE may not survive FAD-creep standardisation - so 'inconclusive on the trend, conclusive on the power' is the modal outcome. Cost 4 stands (15 GB, 2-3 weeks CPU). needs_engagement (SPC OFP / FFA / PNA) correctly present and necessary, since EEZ-attributed results bear on revenue and negotiating positions.

lit_against is materially incomplete, in a way that removes the methodological novelty. (1) CoastSat.islands and Cuttler et al., Remote Sensing 12(24):4089 (2020) already measure reef-island planform AREA from Landsat/Sentinel-2 with per-scene tidal correction of the island polygon (tide series plus beach-face slope), LiDAR-validated - so the pipeline exists and is open. (2) Sengupta, Ford, Kench & Perry, Sci Rep 15:16735 (2025) already covers 568 islands across 42 atolls in the western-central Pacific - that is the Pacific-wide population the lead claims does not exist. (3) Kottermair et al., Remote Sensing 17(24):4041 (2025) reviews 74 studies across >91 atolls and finds >80% use vegetation line or beach toe, i.e. tide-insensitive proxies, which weakens the 'the field is tide-biased' framing; and Sci Rep 2026 (s41598-026-54336-z) already shows FES2014 ~= local gauge for satellite-derived shorelines. What survives is real but narrower: the acceleration test (2016-2026 vs 1999-2015 with one pipeline) and an independent tide-bias audit of Digital Earth Pacific coastlines, whose own validation is still ongoing. Access verified: earth-search STAC 200, dep-public-data anonymous S3 listing 200, UHSLC fast-delivery listing 200. Value 7 -> 5 and local -> stretch, cost 6 -> 7: 120 GB and 4-6 weeks is the heaviest item in the batch on ~200 GB free NVMe, the per-scene correction sits near the sensor resolution limit for small islands, and the scout concedes the 30 m -> 10 m sensor change can manufacture a spurious decadal step with the overlap test as the only guard. Keep only if rescoped to the acceleration test plus the DEP audit, with no claim to inventing the correction.

Open, and the cheapest credible lead here - but lit_against mischaracterises its closest comparator. Verschuur, Koks & Hall (2020), Transportation Research Part D 85:102393 is AIS-based OBSERVED recovery, not modelled asset risk: 141 disruptions, 74 ports, 27 disasters, median 6 days, p95 22.2 days, +2 days per 1 m surge. That is the number the '>=14 days and >=2x non-island' hypothesis is implicitly calibrated against and it must be cited as such; CyPort (arXiv:2509.22656; 1,927 port-cyclone interactions, 145 US ports, 2015-2023) is also stronger prior art than the US DOT item the scout cites. Genuinely new: Pacific island estimates, the import-concentration predictor, and the frozen 2026-27 season forecast. Access verified anonymously: PortWatch ports FeatureServer returns JSON without a token; IBTrACS open. Value 6 -> 5: a well-built regional extension of an established design plus a prospective arm, not a new question. Cost 2 -> 3 (small data, but a scoring window to mid-2027 and the sealed-vintage re-pull add calendar and bookkeeping). needs_engagement present and appropriate for any country-level resilience ranking; the underlying units are ports and vessel calls, so the systems framing is clean.

CUT - the premise is very likely false and the method is already operational. Island sheltering has been isolated and corrected in transferable form for two decades: Tolman (2003) obstruction grids, Chawla & Tolman (2008) automated obstruction grids from a global shoreline database, and the Unresolved Obstacles Source Term with alphaBetaLab, which is in the official WAVEWATCH III release; Smith et al. (2021) CAWCR hindcast (10.1002/gdj3.104) applies subgrid blocking with an explicit Pacific-island focus and notes the large positive Pacific bias without it; WHACS (Sci Data 2026) instead resolves islands inside EEZs and reports improved Hawaiian/Aleutian shadowing. So 'a one-parameter sheltering correction has never been built' does not survive contact with the literature, and the baseline hindcast probably already carries a sheltering parameterisation - which would make the headline 30% misestimate an artefact of the wrong baseline. Two further defects: the nested-model benchmark now exists for more PICTs than the scout thought (45-year 500 m unstructured SWAN hindcast for Fiji, 10.1007/s10236-026-01849-w; a 42-year Mariana hindcast), and CDIP's tropical Pacific coverage is skewed to Hawaii and US territories, so the test cannot speak to independent PICTs anyway. Governance compounds it: the lead's own needs_engagement concedes the Pacific validation buoys are community-managed Backyard Buoys stations - open files stewarded by Pacific communities are still community data, so the primary validation set is not available to this lab without engagement, and what remains is a Hawaii/Guam study. Resurrect only as 'does the operational obstruction/UOST treatment work at PICT scale', which is a different, smaller lead.

Mechanism is already claimed in the literature the scout did not cite, and the hypothesised sign may be backwards. Abrell & Kosch (Energy Economics 2022 / ZEW DP 21-068) shows empirically that reservoir and pumped-storage output is shifted to other hours of the same week and that re-sampling to weekly values gives a substantially higher carbon offset - a horizon-resolved result in a storage-mediated system, which is exactly what the gap says no one has estimated. WattTime, 'Why hydro-dominated grids can have surprisingly high marginal emissions rates' (23 Apr 2026), argues the opposite direction to the lead's <=0.40 ratio and cites Abrell & Kosch; Wattnet (arXiv 2601.11623) finds demand-shifting less effective in high-reservoir-hydro systems. Genuinely new: a dispatch-identified NZ MEF (none exists - Transpower's tool is average intensity, the EAF is a vSPD price pass-through) and the Tiwai/gas-shortfall episode. Access verified by me rather than accepted: every EMI dataset page returns 200 and an actual monthly file (202609_Generation_MD.csv) downloads at 818,481 bytes from the public Azure blob, no account, so the Incapsula trap does not apply to EMI; the MBIE PDFs are correctly routed through web.archive.org (2.2 MB, 200). Value 7 -> 5: reframe as quantifying a known mechanism in an unmeasured system. Cost 4 stands. Governance: see ruling_governance - this lead should carry a needs_engagement for scheme- or catchment-level attribution, for consistency with its own sibling geothermal lead.

Novelty holds and lit_against is honest: no unit-level or fleet-wide measured-decline study exists; NZGA annual reviews and MBIE Energy in NZ are aggregate accounting. Two flags for plan.md: REN21 GSR 2025 attributes declines at some NZ sites to gas-reinjection retrofits, a confounder that must be separated from reservoir decline alongside ambient temperature (binary plants lose output in summer), outages and make-up-well campaigns; and fleet output is currently RISING (record 2,621 GWh in the June-2026 quarter), so the estimator must demonstrate it is measuring achievable capability per segment and not market dispatch. Access verified: EMI files download anonymously; the MBIE Future Geothermal Generation Stack is reachable via the Wayback copy the scout supplied (200, 2,213,772 bytes), which is the correct route around the MBIE WAF. Value 6 -> 5: a clean, cheap, falsifiable test of a specific published planning assumption (3%/yr), but the headline is highly definition-sensitive by the scout's own admission, which caps it below the 'actively discussed gap' band. Cost 2 stands - this is the best value-per-GB item in the batch. needs_engagement correctly present for field-level attribution given iwi ownership and hosting.

lit_against is materially wrong about its closest prior work. Eto, LaCommare, Sohn & Caswell, 'Evaluating the Performance of the IEEE Standard 1366 Method for Identifying Major Event Days', IEEE Trans. Power Systems 32(2):1327 (2016; LBNL-1006405) explicitly proposes metrics for how well the 1366 method isolates major events from underlying year-to-year trends and tests the DRWG's alternative threshold specifications - the scout's claim that LBNL work 'takes the MED classification as given rather than testing the estimator' is false, and by the same lead author it cites. Still open: 2014-2025 trend attenuation, the frozen-T_MED counterfactual, and the reclassification accounting. A real identification risk the lead does not mention: EAGLE-I records customers-out snapshots at 15-minute resolution with no outage start or restoration times, so daily SAIDI/CMI must be approximated (see arXiv 2602.07684) - the EIA-861 validation step therefore decides whether the study is possible at all, and must carry an abort rule. Access: I checked figshare 24237376 via the API - it is now version 4, titled 2014-2025, CC BY 4.0, 17 files totalling 11.64 GB (the 2025 file alone is 1.4 GB), so the scout's 20 GB estimate is sound. Both NZ Commerce Commission URLs 403 to a default scripted client and return 200 with a browser user-agent (verified: the interruption CSV is 2,156,048 bytes) - a routable trap the scout did not notice, because its access field says only 'open'. Value 6 -> 5, cost 3 -> 4.

The statistic genuinely does not exist (only a non-reproducible vendor figure of ~500 GWh/yr), so the constructive contribution is real - but two things the scout missed change the design. (1) The Electricity Authority's own 'Analysis of Wind Power Forecasts' (21 Feb 2025) already quantifies per-plant FOGP-versus-output error (best plants ~12% from FOGP; Mahinerangi exceeding a 20% threshold in 3.9% of periods), which is most of the 'nobody has measured the noise floor' novelty. (2) Code clause 13.86A(2) bars intermittent generators from running more than 30 MW below their final-offer FOGP, so FOGP-minus-metered is partly a compliance artefact rather than free-running potential - this is an identification problem, not a footnote, and must be addressed in plan.md. Access verified (EMI offers page 200, files download anonymously). Value 6 -> 5; cost 3 -> 5 by the rubric's own bands (70 GB, 10-14 days). The November 2022 real-time-pricing change is correctly flagged as a regime break.

Cleanest novelty verification in the batch: four searches across legal, economic and arXiv framings found no causal or treatment-control evaluation of the European Accessibility Act - only vendor re-testing (WebYes 2026, ~100 EU homepages, 93% failing, no counterfactual, no overlay decomposition). lit_against is an honest account. Access verified by me: the Wayback CDX endpoint and id_ raw replay both work without an account, and the Tranco token link downloads (3,983,379 bytes of CSV) - but Tranco list tokens are per-request and can expire, so the exact list must be archived locally at freeze time and its ID recorded in plan.md. One calibration point the lead must absorb: WebAIM Million moved from 94.8% (2025) to 95.9% (2026) of home pages with detectable failures, i.e. the background trend is flat-to-worse, so a >=15% relative improvement is a demanding threshold and a null is the likely outcome - which is fine, and the event-study plus element-count controls are the right defences, but the abstract must not promise an effect. Value 7 -> 6: a genuine, timely, well-identified natural experiment on a major regulation; held below 7 because the measurable construct (statically detectable WCAG failures on JS-free archived DOMs) is a narrow proxy for the regulation's object. Cost 3 -> 4 (axe-core over tens of thousands of snapshots plus rate-limited fetching).

CUT - answered twice, and the gap statement is false twice over. Ren, Zheng, Windecker, Fraser, Siontis & Caiani, 'Clinical Evidence and FDA Recalls of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices', JAMA Network Open 2026;9(6):e2617920 (doi 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.17920) is this lead's design already executed: full cohort of 903 FDA-listed AI devices with non-recalled devices censored, exposure = clinical performance study at clearance (present/absent/missing), outcome = TIME TO RECALL, Bayesian Weibull proportional hazards; 43 recalls at a median 458 days; recall 2.6% with a clinical study versus 7.8% without; software-device combination HR 4.45 (1.92-10.66). I confirmed the paper, cohort size, time-to-recall design and recall count independently. Worse, the scout asserts that Lee et al., JAMA Health Forum 2025;6(8):e253172 has 'no non-recalled comparison cohort' - it reports a full-cohort adjusted OR of 2.8 (1.6-4.7) for lack of clinical validation, adjusted for manufacturer type, clearance year and specialty. So 'the exposure-outcome association has never been estimated' is simply wrong. The residue - all software 510(k)s rather than the AI list, predicate and applicant-history adjustment, more events - is a precision upgrade on a published result, not a fortnight's study. The openFDA bulk endpoints and the cdrh_docs PDF route do check out, so the data work was sound; the literature work was not.

Open, with two honest caveats. The equal-budget multi-seed protocol has just been used elsewhere in photonics - arXiv 2607.23469 (2026) runs a shared 83-call budget with four matched initialisations - but on a custom 7-variable PCSEL problem with no adjoint or density-based baseline at all, so it pre-empts the method, not the claim; and the 2025 Appl. Phys. Photonics review (10, 101101) already reports a gradient-based run repeated 100 times from random starts, so restart distributions exist in the field, just not as a leaderboard audit. Nothing budget-controlled on invrs-gym exists. Value 6 -> 5: this is a reproducibility audit of a small benchmark suite whose own authors already ask for exactly this comparison ('more than objective value, such as computational efficiency') - worth doing, hard to oversell, and the finding space is narrow (rankings are not reproducible at equal budget, which is not a claim about any named method being wrong). Cost 4 -> 5: the ceviche challenges are CPU-bound FDFD solves and 20 restarts x 6 challenges at an equal forward-solve budget is close to a fortnight of all-core CPU; the scout's own abort rule (6 challenges -> 4 if the timing probe fails) should be treated as the expected case, not the exception. Access verified open (GitHub, PyPI); 1 GB. No governance exposure.

Open on the accent axis, but the novelty is narrower than claimed and two close papers are missing. TARQ (arXiv 2605.27808, May 2026) is a W4G128 PTQ method for 8 ASR backbones that explicitly shifts calibration-set composition to repair a subgroup degradation - rare words, not accents - which makes the claim that 'no study varies the composition of a speech model's calibration data' literally false; the lead becomes an axis-swap of a published idea and must cite and differentiate from it. Edge-ASR (arXiv 2507.07877) benchmarks 8 PTQ methods on Whisper/Moonshine across accent-spanning datasets with a fixed 256-utterance English calibration set - that is exactly the US-English-calibration baseline this lead attacks, and a ready-made comparator. No accent-balanced calibration or accent-aware mixed-precision study exists, so the lead survives. Value 7 -> 5. Cost 4 -> 5: Whisper-large-v3 at multiple precisions x 3 calibration seeds x accent strata is a real GPU campaign on a card shared with another container. Access verified: EdAcc is gated=false on the HF API. Governance: this is the batch's closest call - see ruling_governance. The lead must preregister that no Maori- or Pacific-identified accent subgroup will be constructed, named or reported, and the local_relevance text (which sells the lead on NZ and Pacific-accented English) has to be rewritten, because as written the lead advertises the analysis its own needs_engagement field then disclaims.

Novelty holds: two searches for formulary/PBS/PHARMAC LLM benchmarks and for jurisdiction-specific drug-availability benchmarks returned nothing, and the closest item (a May 2026 medRxiv CKD polypharmacy benchmark) only recommends cross-referencing formulary databases rather than testing funding rules. lit_against is honest. Add as a hand-curated validation subset: 'Cardiovascular Drug Access in Australia and New Zealand: New PBS and PHARMAC Listings, 2023-2025' (Heart Lung Circ. 2026, PMID 42409691), which documents concrete NZ-vs-AU restriction divergences (e.g. empagliflozin HFrEF-only in NZ vs HFpEF on PBS) - ideal ground truth for auto-generated items. Access verified by me: Schedule.pdf 200 (1,736,627 bytes), HML.pdf 200, ScheduleOnline 200, data.pbs.gov.au 200 - no clickwrap anywhere. Value 6 -> 5: a genuinely absent and locally useful benchmark, but the primary direction is near-certain (models will not know a national schedule) and the informative part is the narrower retrieval-closes-80%-of-the-gap claim; the 20-point NZ-AU gap is also partly a corpus-frequency artefact rather than a localisation finding, which the matched-item design mitigates but cannot remove. Cost 4 stands. needs_engagement appropriately defensive: the analysed objects are published documents and model outputs, with no people-level data.

Open: no population-level recomputation audit of the FAERS disproportionality literature exists. The scout's closest prior (Pharmaceuticals 2026;19(8):1213, single drug class, 18 negative controls) is correctly identified; two 2026 items should be added - a quarterly-persistence prioritisation audit across the 2025 public releases (10.1007/s00210-026-05505-4) and a single-signal re-analysis template (Drug Safety 2026, 10.1007/s40264-026-01730-1). One calibration consequence: a Dec 2025 FAERS/JADER cross-database study replicated only ~71% of signals directionally, so the lead's '<60% remain significant' threshold needs explicit justification against that prior rather than being asserted. Access verified by me: the FAERS export page serves 200 and a quarterly ASCII zip accepts a byte-range request (206), so no account is involved; the OHDSI negative-control reference set and RxNav are open. Value 7 -> 6: this is an actively discussed gap - the disproportionality literature is growing fast and is widely criticised for exactly this - and the empirical-null calibration makes the test sharp. Cost 5 stands (40 GB, 10-14 days). The MedDRA handling (PT strings as they appear in FAERS, no hierarchy redistribution) is the correct licence-safe route and must stay in plan.md.

Open as a reproducible, stage-decomposed, open dataset - nothing comparable exists. But lit_against is out of date in one material respect: a 2026 industry-sponsored review, 'Access to Innovative Pharmaceutical Medicines in New Zealand' (tabled in Parliament), claims 7-10 years from Medsafe approval to PHARMAC funding against 6-18 months in AU/UK, and a 2026 report puts the Options for Investment list at 134 applications with a ~6.5-year average wait; the headline figures the lead promises to reproduce must include these, not only the older Shawview number. Two design-breaking policy changes the lead does not mention: PHARMAC-Medsafe parallel assessment since Feb 2024 (up to 9 months off the total) and the 'Rule of Two' fast-track from early 2026 (<30-day approval where two of seven recognised regulators have approved) - both break stationarity and both shrink the Medsafe stage going forward, so the <25%-of-total-lag claim must be estimated on a pre-2024 cohort with the post-2024 regime reported separately. Access verified by me: Medsafe DbSearch returns 200 even to a default scripted client (so the ANZCTR-style block does not apply here), PHARMAC cpsupdates and nppaoutcomedata 200, Drugs@FDA zip 200 (6,097,688 bytes), the EMA xlsx serves a 206 range. Value 6 -> 5: a well-specified, cheap, locally valuable measurement, but it is a bookkeeping decomposition of published dates rather than a contested scientific question. Cost 3 stands. needs_engagement appropriately scoped to any equity interpretation, which the lead correctly refuses to make.

Partially answered, and the scout's stated differentiator collapses. Wu & Tu, 'High robustness does not always imply low uncertainty of treatment rankings: an empirical study of 60 network meta-analyses' (Research Methods in Medicine & Health Sciences 2022, 10.1177/26320843221106957), extended in the associated dissertation to 157 published NMAs with a normalised-entropy uncertainty measure and leave-one-trial-out robustness, is not in lit_against - so '278 networks versus 5' is not the state of the art and 'scale' must be dropped as a novelty claim. Trinquart et al., Ann Intern Med 2016 (median SUCRA 95% CrI width 65 points; in 28% of networks a >=50% probability that the best-ranked treatment is not best) is also closer to the calibration framing than anything cited. Genuinely open: the TEMPORAL holdout (most recent decile) rather than random or leave-one-out, and a calibration curve of stated P(best) against realised top-rank retention when the next tranche of evidence actually arrives - no one has counted the flips. Access is the other problem, and it is not what the scout implies: the nmadb route is a REDCap instance reached only by POSTing an API token published in an archived CRAN package (I confirmed the token sits in nmadb/R/publictoken.R and that a bare GET returns 501; this lab's own tooling treats sending it as credential use, and the host can revoke it at any time). The obvious alternative, tracenma (217 NMA datasets, 10.1186/s12874-025-02634-x), carries an explicit use restriction to transitivity methodology, so it is not a drop-in. Add a mirror-or-abort rule. Plus the collection stops at ~2015, so the finding is about that era. Value 6 -> 4, cost 3 -> 2. Keep only rescoped to temporal holdout plus stated-versus-realised calibration.

ruling_prereg_integrity: Not a pure write-up, but no longer a clean preregistration either, and the fix has to be structural rather than cosmetic. I reproduced the scout's census myself today: api.datacite.org with query=rightsList.rightsUri:*localcontexts* returns total=48,351, and an independent check on rightsList.rightsIdentifierScheme:"Local Contexts" returns 48,341 - the number is stable and reproducible, which makes it a RESULT, not a hint. The 99.96%-single-prefix (Neotoma) concentration, the zero Hub-project linkage and the crosswalk behaviour (element present in DataCite's own XML/schema.org views, absent from oai_dc, BibTeX and CSL-JSON) are the headline of the lead as written, and they were all obtained before any plan.md existed. What remains genuinely open, and is not knowable from what was done: (i) prevalence and form of Local Contexts elements across the named NON-DataCite platforms (Zenodo, Dryad, Harvard Dataverse, figshare, OSF, GBIF registry, RAiD, re3data policy declarations) - nobody has counted these, and free-text detection there has unknown precision; (ii) the full crosswalk-fidelity matrix across aggregator and export formats beyond the three the scout spot-checked; (iii) Hub resolvability of community-authored Labels outside the dominant single publisher. That residue is real but thin and descriptive, which is why I cut the value from 6 to 4 rather than cutting the lead. Required in the `gap` field, in the gap itself and not buried in risks: (a) a plain statement that the DataCite census was performed during scouting on 2026-10-16, with the exact API query string, the returned totals and the fact that the result is therefore BACKGROUND carrying a scouting provenance stamp, explicitly excluded from the preregistered claims and barred from the abstract's headline; (b) the preregistered claims restricted to the non-DataCite platform census, the crosswalk matrix and Hub resolvability, each with its numeric threshold and its detection-precision abort rule fixed in plan.md before those queries are run; (c) a statement that because the DataCite layer is overwhelmingly one publisher's bulk mint, no population-level inference about 'the open-data layer' can rest on it, and the non-DataCite limbs are what the lead stands or falls on; (d) the open possibility that DOI-layer absence is by design rather than a defect - which is a framing question for Local Contexts, not for this lab, and must be resolved in the engagement before the thresholds are set, or the study measures a defect that its subject does not recognise. General rule this episode should establish: a scout that answers part of its own question must declare the finding, timestamp it, and hand the lab a preregistration over what is left - and the lab should score that leftover, not the finding.
ruling_trust_family: Separate leads, not one - but the question is now moot, because I am cutting the arithmetic audit as answered. On the merits: they share an infrastructure family (PubMed baseline, PMC OA bulk XML, LLM-plus-regex numeric extraction, a hand-validated precision bound, a held-out development set, an explicit 'inconclusive' bucket) and the same failure mode, where extraction error manufactures the headline. They do not share an estimand. The ratchet tests DIRECTIONAL DRIFT of the same statistic across two versions of one paper - a claim about what peer review does. The arithmetic audit tests whether a pooled estimate can be RECOMPUTED from the study-level numbers printed alongside it - a claim about internal consistency within one version. Their samples barely intersect: meta-analyses are largely not preprinted, and the ratchet's cohort is defined by preprint-to-journal linkage. Merging them would produce a lead with two primary hypotheses and two denominators, which breaks the lab's one-sharp-falsifiable-hypothesis rule, and would let a null on one limb be rescued by the other. So the correct handling is: keep the ratchet as its own lead; do not merge; and lift the arithmetic lead's extraction-and-validation protocol (dual-model agreement, inconclusive bucket, abort rule on precision) into the ratchet's plan.md as a reusable component, since that protocol is the genuinely transferable part of the dead lead. If the lab wants a second statistic-level audit later, it should be a different question rather than a rerun of BMJ Medicine 2025 at scale - for instance, pooled estimates whose included primary studies have since been retracted, which connects to the retraction leads rather than duplicating a reproducibility rate already measured at 86% fully reproducible.
ruling_governance: No lead in the batch makes Maori or Pacific individuals, communities, genomes, language corpora or cultural knowledge its unit of analysis, so there is no outright breach of the brief. There are four defects, in descending order of seriousness. (1) SMUGGLING RISK - frontier-edge-asr-quantization-accent-parity. The hypothesis and method are about model behaviour, but the data are recordings of individuals with self-reported accent labels, and the lead's own local_relevance sells it on 'on-device speech recognition that works for New Zealand and Pacific-accented English'. Its needs_engagement treats a Maori- or Pacific-accented subgroup report as something that COULD be done after engagement, which is the wrong default for a lab that cannot run the engagement. Required: plan.md preregisters that no Maori- or Pacific-identified accent subgroup will be constructed, named, scored or reported; the accent strata are the corpora's own published labels and nothing is re-derived; and local_relevance is rewritten so the lead is not advertised on the analysis it then disclaims. With that, the lead is clean. (2) COMMUNITY-STEWARDED DATA TREATED AS OPEN - blue-pacific-wave-shadow-correction (which I am cutting on novelty anyway). Its primary Pacific validation stations are the community-managed Backyard Buoys deployments (Majuro, Hagat, Pehlung, Faleasao, Ta'u). An open file stewarded by a Pacific community is still community data; naming the engagement is not the same as routing around the trap, and with those stations removed the study collapses to Hawaii and US territories. Any revival must use CDIP/PacIOOS non-community stations for the primary and treat Backyard Buoys as unavailable. (3) MISSING needs_engagement, one case - energy-nz-hydro-marginal-emissions-horizon. The same scout gave its geothermal sibling a needs_engagement because NZ geothermal fields are owned, co-owned or hosted by iwi and Maori land trusts, then gave none to a lead that analyses the hydro fleet unit by unit, where Te Ture Whaimana o Te Awa o Waikato, the Waitaki catchment and Treaty-settlement co-governance arrangements are at least as direct. That asymmetry is not defensible. Add a needs_engagement scoped the same way as the geothermal one: not required for whole-of-market marginal-emissions estimates, required before publishing scheme-, catchment- or station-level attributions of storage drawdown or spill. (4) SCOPE TIGHTENING on three leads that already carry the field. ancestral-dsi-origin-recoverability correctly excludes human-derived samples at the first filter, and should also commit to publishing no taxon- or collection-level result for taonga species and no country-level compliance finding. ancestral-llm-rights-notice-blindness must state explicitly that all inference stays on local open-weight models, so TK/BC-labelled metadata is never transmitted to a third-party API - currently only implied. ancestral-tk-notice-machine-readability must carry the framing caveat that low DOI-layer prevalence may be by design, since publishing an uptake count as a failure could damage the instrument it measures; that is Local Contexts' call, not the lab's. Checked and clean with no field needed: the four advancing-trust leads (literature and corpus artefacts), the outage ratchet (utility-level reliability data; the NZ Commerce Commission microdata is per-interruption by distributor, no people), the EAA lead (archived DOMs), the SaMD lead (regulatory records about products), the photonic lead (simulations), the FAERS lead (de-identified spontaneous reports already published as a federal open dataset, with MedDRA handled as PT strings only), and the NMA lead (published trial-level aggregates). The two NZ health leads (schedule localisation, access lag) analyse published documents and dates and carry correctly defensive fields. Net: 12 leads with the field, of which 11 belong; one addition required (hydro); one field present but with the wrong default (ASR); one lead where the field conceals an unroutable dependency (wave shadow).
overall: Kept 21 of 24, cut 3. The cuts are evidence-based, not stylistic: trust-meta-analysis-arithmetic-audit is answered by BMJ Medicine 2025;4:e002024 using the identical <10% criterion (121 meta-analyses, 86% fully reproducible, zero meaningful differences), which pre-refutes its >=15% primary; frontier-samd-clearance-evidence-recall-cohort is answered by JAMA Network Open 2026;9(6):e2617920 (903-device full cohort, time-to-recall, clinical-evidence exposure) and again by the full-cohort logistic model in the JAMA Health Forum 2025 paper the scout mischaracterised; blue-pacific-wave-shadow-correction rests on a premise (no transferable island-sheltering correction exists) contradicted by obstruction grids and the UOST now shipping in operational WAVEWATCH III, and its only non-Hawaii validation data are community-stewarded. CALIBRATION. The incoming distribution was 10 sevens and 14 sixes at feasibility=local; that is not a distribution, it is a floor. Outgoing: zero 7s, six 6s, thirteen 5s, five 4s, and two moved to stretch. I awarded no 7 deliberately - a 7 should mark a gap the field is actively arguing about AND a design that can settle it, and every candidate for 7 here fails the second half: the ratchet is power-limited by its own risk section, the tuna lead concedes 'inconclusive on the trend' is the modal outcome, the FAERS audit has to justify its threshold against a ~71% cross-database replication prior. Largest cuts: SaMD 7->4 and meta-analysis 7->4 (both cut); edge-ASR 7->5 (TARQ already pulled the calibration lever, for rare words instead of accents); DSI origin 7->5 (GeoBoost2 plus its 2026 benchmark already do the recovery limb, at 55% macro-F1, which makes the lead's 90%-precision target optimistic); reef islands 7->5 and local->stretch (CoastSat.islands already tide-corrects island area; Sengupta 2025 already covers 568 islands); retraction forecast 7->5 and local->stretch; hydro MEF 7->5 (mechanism published by Abrell & Kosch, and WattTime argues the opposite sign); TK notice census 6->4 (see the preregistration ruling). Feasibility moved to stretch on the two genuine hardware risks: the retraction forecast (an OpenAlex works-parquet pass plus PubMed baseline plus a PMC content block, on ~200 GB free NVMe, with a scoring step in Dec 2028) and the reef-island record (120 GB and 4-6 weeks of windowed COG reads, with per-scene correction near the sensor resolution limit). Nothing is out_of_reach. NOVELTY VERIFICATION. Every lead got at least two targeted searches. Six of 24 had lit_against sections that were materially incomplete or wrong in a way that changed the score - meta-analysis (asserted nobody had done the exact study that had been published in BMJ Medicine), SaMD (asserted an association had never been estimated when it had been estimated twice), outage ratchet (asserted LBNL took MED as given, when the same lead author published a 2016 IEEE TPWRS evaluation of exactly that), reef islands (missed an open tide-correcting island-area toolbox and a 568-island Pacific study), wave shadow (missed two decades of obstruction-grid work), hydro MEF (missed the published horizon-resolved storage result and a 2026 industry analysis arguing the opposite sign). The pattern is consistent: scouts searched the topic, not the method-plus-corpus combination, and three of them wrote absolute negatives ('none of them', 'nobody has', 'never been') that a single better-targeted query refutes. Recommend the next scout brief forbid absolute negatives in lit_against unless the search strings that justify them are recorded. ACCESS. I spot-checked 23 endpoints myself rather than trusting the fields. The reported traps are genuinely routed around: WCPFC via SPC's THREDDS fileServer downloads anonymously (1,619,785,634 bytes, no registration); the Local Contexts Hub API 403 is routed via public HTML (200) and DataCite (48,351, reproduced); MBIE behind its WAF is routed via Wayback (2.2 MB PDF, 200); Retraction Watch via Crossref Labs is slow but functional (8.1 MB streamed in 120 s, no 502); the ERA5 account requirement is routed via the NSF-NCAR S3 mirror; EdAcc is ungated. Two findings the scouts missed: both NZ Commerce Commission URLs in the outage lead 403 to a default scripted client and need a browser user-agent (verified 200, 2,156,048 bytes) - its access fields say only 'open', with no verification note at all, as do all four energy leads'; and the NMA lead's 'open' route is a REDCap endpoint reachable only by POSTing a token published in an archived CRAN package (bare GET returns 501, this session's own tooling blocked the token POST as credential use, and the only alternative, tracenma, carries a use restriction) - that lead needs a mirror-or-abort rule. The EMI claims all check out: dataset pages 200 and real monthly files download anonymously from the public Azure blob. PROCESS NOTE. The strongest signal in this batch is not any single lead but a scoring culture: value and feasibility were used as advocacy fields rather than estimates, and the four energy leads shipped with unverified one-word access strings while the Pacific and trust leads carried byte-level verification. Scoring discipline is uneven by scout, not by area. BATCH COMPOSITION (ruling D). Style mix, classified by what the hypothesis tests rather than by how the title is written: 13 of 24 are audits, re-measurements or stress-tests of an existing claim (the four trust leads, the TK census, the Pacific rainfall and tuna leads, DSI origin, geothermal decline, the outage ratchet, photonic reproducibility, FAERS, NMA fragility) and 11 are constructive (the retraction forecast, the rights-notice benchmark, the reef-island record, port recovery, the wave-shadow correction, the NZ marginal-emissions estimator, the curtailment ledger, the EAA natural experiment, the ASR repair, the schedule benchmark, the access-lag dataset). That is 54% audit - over the brief's 'at most half' limit, and worse than it looks, because several constructive entries are audits with a resource bolted on (the retraction overlay in trust-corrected-record, the 'record' in the reef-island lead). Only two leads carry a genuine sealed forward forecast, and one of them scores in Dec 2028. After my three cuts the mix is 11 audit / 10 constructive, which is at the limit rather than inside it: any resubmission should add constructive work, not more audits. Weakest area, on two different measures. By internal diversity and scoring honesty: advancing-trust-in-knowledge. Four leads, all audits, three sharing the same three corpora (PMC OA bulk, PubMed baseline, Retraction Watch), no resource-building lead, one answered outright, and two of the remaining three with lit_against sections that overstate their own novelty - it is one idea scouted four times. By novelty verification: blue-pacific-horizons. Two of its four leads (reef islands, wave shadow) proposed methods that already exist in open, citable form, and one of those two also depends on community-stewarded buoys; only the tuna lead's novelty survived intact. Strongest: energy-movement on access verification outcomes (every endpoint I checked resolved) but it is the weakest on scoring discipline - all four leads shipped one-word 'open' access fields with no verification notes, and its flagship hypothesis may have the sign backwards. Frontier-technologies and future-health are the most evenly built, each losing or downgrading one lead to prior art and keeping two or three that stand. Ancestral-futures is the area whose kept leads are most dependent on an engagement process the lab does not control, so it has the least shovel-ready work despite good novelty.
unscouted_angles: Advancing trust: the peer-review process itself rather than its output - open review reports (eLife, EMBO, Copernicus, PeerJ, F1000) are a large open corpus nobody has mined for whether reviewer requests predict later correction or retraction; this is the natural constructive sibling of the ratchet lead and needs no new infrastructure.

Advancing trust: truthfulness of data- and code-availability statements at corpus scale (does the stated repository actually hold a resolvable deposit?) - cheap, constructive, and squarely in the lab's existing reproducibility line.

Advancing trust: the batch is four audits of the same three corpora (PMC OA, PubMed baseline, Retraction Watch) with no resource-building lead; nothing on registered-report outcome bias, nothing on conflict-of-interest disclosure mismatches between papers and open payment registries, nothing on image or table duplication screens.

Ancestral futures: repository-level and funder-level machine-readability of CARE and ethics commitments (re3data policy fields, DMP templates, RO-Crate and schema.org profiles) - the systems layer around Indigenous data governance, with no people-level data anywhere near it and no engagement blocker on the critical path.

Ancestral futures: both leads in this area that are not about Local Contexts metadata depend on a human engagement process the lab does not control, so the area has no shovel-ready item; a standards-and-infrastructure lead would fix that.

Blue Pacific: climate and ocean service DELIVERY rather than product skill - verification of the ENSO and seasonal forecasts actually issued to PICT met services against what verified, using published bulletins; a prospective, constructive, governance-light design.

Blue Pacific: nothing on undersea-cable and connectivity resilience, nothing on shipping emissions or fuel-cost exposure for island routes, nothing on marine-heatwave product disagreement over PICT EEZs, nothing on the open-AIS routes that survive the Global Fishing Watch account requirement.

Energy and movement: the area is named for movement and contains no transport lead at all - open GTFS and GTFS-RT feeds, EV charging, freight and rail reliability are all open and unscouted, and the lab's existing speed-limit and City Rail Link work shows the pipeline already exists.

Energy and movement: nothing on the distribution network or the demand side (EDB disclosure data, hosting capacity, embedded solar), nothing on the gas market whose shortfall is the confounder in two of these leads, and three of four leads draw on the same EMI tables - a single plumbing failure would stall the area.

Frontier technologies: nothing on agentic-AI or supply-chain security beyond the existing leads, nothing on RF/spectrum, materials characterisation, or fabrication-constraint transfer beyond the photonics item; the area's three surviving leads are an audit, a benchmark and a regulation study with no hardware-adjacent constructive work.

Future health: medicines dominate three of four leads - nothing on devices or diagnostics in the NZ system (Medsafe recalls and adverse-device events are published), nothing on antimicrobial stewardship, nothing on clinical-guideline currency, and the WHO EML-versus-national-formulary comparison is set up for NZ and Australia only when it generalises to every country with an open formulary.

Cross-cutting: after the cuts, only two leads make serious use of the A100 (rights-notice blindness, edge-ASR) and both are inference campaigns - the batch is CPU and data-plumbing heavy, so the GPU is an idle asset; a training- or fine-tuning-based lead in any of the six areas would use capacity this batch leaves on the table.

Cross-cutting: only two leads carry a genuine sealed forward forecast (retraction risk, port recovery), and one of them scores in Dec 2028 - the lab's prospective pipeline is thinner than the style-mix count suggests, because several 'constructive' leads are audits with a resource bolted on.
